sentences.text: Rhamphinion is a genus of pterosaurs whose name means "beak nape" because the fossils come from the rear of the skull.
Rhamphinion was once the oldest known pterosaur from the Western Hemisphere, a record now held by Caelestiventus.
Fossils of Rhamphinion were discovered in 1978 in Coconino County, northern Arizona, by an expedition led by Farish A. Jenkins Jr.
The holotype specimen consists of fragmentary remains from a single individual, including two skull fragments, a possible jaw fragment, and an unidentifiable bone impression.
Rhamphinion jenkinsi was described and named in 1984 by Kevin Padian based on the holotype specimen MNA.V.4500.
In its original description, Kevin Padian did not assign Rhamphinion to a specific family but suggested it might be a basal pterosaur based on its jugal bone.
Kevin Padian noted that the jugal bone of Rhamphinion differed from pterodactyloids, suggesting it might belong to a basal pterosaur group called rhamphorhynchoids.
While Peter Wellnhofer considered Rhamphinion likely to be a rhamphorhynchoid, David Unwin classified it as a possibly valid species with uncertain relationships.
Peter Wellnhofer agreed that Rhamphinion was likely a rhamphorhynchoid, whereas David Unwin remained hesitant, calling it a possibly valid species with uncertain relationships.
Rhamphinion lived during the Sinemurian to mid-Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic in the Kayenta Formation of northeastern Arizona.
Rhamphinion lived between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago.
